bib.title: Conditional Image Generation with PixelCNN Decoders

question: Can a PixelCNN be improved to match PixelRNN likelihoods and be conditioned on arbitrary vectors to generate and decode images?
hypothesis: Gated activations and a two-stack design close the gap to PixelRNN at lower compute; conditioning on a latent vector gives controllable, diverse images.
contributions: Gated PixelCNN: gated activation units replace ReLU
Two stacks (horizontal and vertical) remove the receptive-field blind spot
Conditional PixelCNN conditioned on class labels or embeddings
PixelCNN as decoder in an autoencoder

method.summary: Masked-convolution autoregressive image model with gated tanh*sigmoid units and horizontal/vertical stacks; conditioning vector h added inside the gates. Evaluated by NLL on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, and qualitatively for class, portrait-embedding and autoencoder uses.
method.task: autoregressive image density modelling and conditional image generation

datasets.name: Flickr portraits
datasets.source: portraits automatically cropped from Flickr images using a face detector

models.name: Gated PixelCNN (ImageNet)
models.architecture: masked-conv autoregressive, gated units, residual in horizontal stack only

other.colour_order: R, then G given R, then B given R,G

training.objective: negative log-likelihood (bits/dim) of the pixel product of conditionals; autoencoder trained end-to-end

other.scope: 20 layers, 384 units, 5x5 filters stated for the Table 2 ImageNet model only

inference.decoding: sequential pixel-by-pixel sampling from softmax, each sampled pixel fed back
inference.samples: multiple conditional reconstructions per input in Fig 6; count not stated

other.interpolation: same random seed per row for smooth transitions

metrics.name: NLL
metrics.definition: negative log-likelihood per dimension on test set (train in brackets)

eval.protocol: Single reported number per model; no seeds or error bars; architectures optimised for validation score; qualitative samples for conditional experiments.

evidence.quote: We used 200K synchronous updates over 32 GPUs in TensorFlow [1] using a total batch size of 128.

results.claim: Gated PixelCNN reaches 3.03 bits/dim test NLL on CIFAR-10, close to PixelRNN.
results.setup: CIFAR-10, Gated PixelCNN, architecture tuned for validation score; test NLL
results.table: Table 1, row Gated PixelCNN, column NLL Test (Train)

results.claim: Gated PixelCNN improves on the original PixelCNN by 0.11 bits/dim on CIFAR-10.
results.setup: CIFAR-10, Gated PixelCNN, architecture tuned for validation score; test NLL
results.quote: Gated PixelCNN outperforms the PixelCNN by 0.11 bits/dim

results.claim: On ImageNet 32x32 Gated PixelCNN gets 3.83 test NLL, beating PixelRNN.
On ImageNet 64x64 Gated PixelCNN gets 3.57 test NLL, beating PixelRNN.
Similar performance to PixelRNN (Row LSTM) in under half the training time.
results.quote: We were able to achieve similar performance to the PixelRNN (Row LSTM [30]) in less than half the training time (60 hours using 32 GPUs).

results.claim: Class conditioning on ImageNet gave no big log-likelihood change but greatly improved visual sample quality.
results.setup: Class-conditional Gated PixelCNN, one-hot over 1000 classes
results.quote: however we did not observe big differences. On the other hand, as noted in [27], we observed great improvements in the visual quality of the generated samples.

results.claim: Class label carries about 0.003 bits/pixel of information for a 32x32 image.
results.note: log(1000)/3072 is about 0.003 only in bits if log base 2 (9.97/3072=0.00324); paper does not state the base

results.claim: Embedding-conditioned model generates varied new portraits of the same person from a single unseen image.
results.setup: Flickr portraits, triplet-loss embedding as h
results.quote: the generative model is able to produce a large variety of new faces with these features in new poses, lighting conditions, etc.

results.claim: PixelCNN decoder in an autoencoder yields qualitatively different bottleneck information than an MSE decoder.
results.quote: the information encoded in the bottleneck representation h will be qualitatively different with a PixelCNN decoder
